sections.title: Encoding helpers — bytes32 → base64url and bytes8 → ASCII
sections.key_moment: base64url is NOT base64. The aggregator URL must use `-` instead of `+`, `_` instead of `/`, and DROP the `=` padding. `btoa()` produces standard base64; getting the substitutions wrong by one character returns 404 silently — the aggregator interprets the wrong slug as an unknown blob, not as a malformed request.

sections.title: The on-chain read — viem PublicClient + ABI
sections.key_moment: Declaring `WALRUS_RESOLVER_ABI as const` (a `const` assertion) is what makes viem type-check the return shape. Without `as const`, the ABI is widened to `any[]` and `readContract` returns `unknown` — the destructuring `[blobId, , contentTypeRaw]` would silently lose type safety. The `as const` is load-bearing TypeScript, not aesthetic style.

sections.title: Aggregator GET + content-type gating
sections.key_moment: The `contentType.startsWith("app/json")` check before the fetch is what prevents a misconfigured pointer (say, one that points at a PNG) from being parsed as JSON downstream. The `bytes8` on-chain field is intentionally a shortcode grammar ("app/json", "text/md", "image/p"), not a full MIME — long MIMEs like "application/json" don't fit eight bytes, which the resolver contract designed in. The client mirrors the design by accepting the shortcode form ONLY.

sections.title: Generic resolveManifest + typed convenience wrapper
sections.key_moment: `resolveTokenList = (name, opts) => resolveManifest<UniswapTokenList>(name, opts)` — the curried specialization is one line and zero runtime overhead. The TYPE narrows at the call site; the implementation stays generic over any JSON shape. This is the cheapest possible 'typed API surface' in TypeScript and it scales to any number of well-known manifest shapes without forcing every caller to specify `<T>` inline.
